key_concepts: A rope moved up and down creates transverse waves that travel along the rope.
Water in a bottle moved back and forth shows transverse wave-like movements.
Dropping a coin on water produces waves that spread outward from the disturbance.
A floating object bobs in place as water waves pass rather than moving along with the wave
Increasing the speed of up-and-down rope motion increases the frequency of the waves.
Regular water waves are produced by wind.
Tsunamis are produced by sudden displacement of water, such as by undersea earthquakes.
Tsunamis differ from regular water waves in cause and scale.
Electromagnetic waves are grouped into regions such as radio waves.
Radio waves are used for telecommunication.
